title: LOB, Over ? Level 1
subtitle: Texas, 3,000 ft, three crews and one collapse.

plan._derivation: no-event push finish t 17.7 (pipe 1 + 3000/180); budget 18 x $4,800 x 1.3 + $60,000; deadline 18 + 12

defaultIndicator.wall: Stiff clay, vertical cut holding. Spoil pile set back about 2 ft.

indicator.wall: Clay softening toward the toe; a thumb goes in. Small slabs have let go near the bottom.
indicator.water: Water seeping from the lower wall; a puddle is forming along the toe.

card.title: Trench wall collapse at 5+20
facts: The lower wall has slumped into the pipe crew's working section.
Pipe crew is out of the trench.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. Three thousand feet, three crews. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised the city Day 18, so keep everybody moving.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You're holding a crew? We promised Day 18. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That's the run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: Wall's moving! Out of the hole, everybody out, now!

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: Okay. Everybody's out, nobody's hurt. That whole side let go at five-twenty, and there's water coming in at the bottom.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: I'm not putting a man back down there until somebody cleans that up.

turns.speaker: foreman_back
turns.text: Marcus, why is your crew standing on the bank? I've got a loader full of dirt and nowhere to put it.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: Because my wall's in the ditch, Dana. Push dirt onto my bedding and you can explain it to the inspector.

turns.speaker: foreman_back
turns.text: The schedule had me here today. I lay two-fifty a day. You lay one-eighty on a good day.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: Then the schedule was wrong before the wall ever moved. Somebody tell the office.

turns.speaker: foreman_back
turns.text: Marcus, I'm on your heels again. Pick it up or get out of my way.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: I lay one-eighty a day, Dana, same as every day. You lay two-fifty. Do the math.

turns.speaker: foreman_back
turns.text: The math says I sit here and get paid to watch you.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: Take it up with whoever wrote the start dates.

turns.speaker: foreman_pipe
turns.text: I heard you the first time.

lines.speaker: foreman_exc
lines.text: Morning, inspector. Good ground today. We'll make our footage if nobody bothers us.

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: Nothing to lay until that wall's cleaned up. My guys are standing around.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Dirt's going in fine. Just keep me fed.

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: Pipe's going in. One-eighty a day if the walls behave.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: We're right on Marcus's heels. Nothing to fill until he lays more pipe.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.
